name: TPS563206DRLR
title: TPS563203, TPS563206: 4.2 V to 17 V input, 3 A synchronous buck converters in SOT563
summary: Two synchronous step-down converters with both power NFETs on chip (100 mΩ high side, 55 mΩ low side), delivering up to 3 A from a 4.2 V to 17 V supply in a 1.6 mm × 1.6 mm, six-pin SOT563 (DRL) package. The output is set by a divider to a 0.6 V feedback reference, from 0.6 V to 7 V. A D-CAP3 adaptive on-time loop runs at about 600 kHz, needs no external compensation and is stable with ceramic or polymer output capacitors. The TPS563203 drops into Eco-mode pulse skipping at light load; the TPS563206 stays in forced continuous conduction (FCCM) at every load for a near-constant frequency and lower ripple. Soft start is fixed at 1.4 ms, and the parts carry cycle-by-cycle valley current limit, undervoltage hiccup, UVLO and thermal shutdown.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: The bare buck stage around either device: an input capacitor on VIN, a bootstrap capacitor from BST to SW, an inductor and output capacitor forming the filter from SW, a two-resistor divider from the output down to FB, and EN brought out as a control input.

circuits.title: TPS563203 1.05 V, 3 A reference design
circuits.description: A 1.05 V, 3 A converter running from 4.2 V to 17 V, the circuit of the evaluation module. C1 and C2 (10 µF) decouple the input and C3 (0.1 µF) adds high-frequency bypass. C7 feeds the high-side gate driver from the switch node. L1 (2.2 µH) with C8 and C9 (22 µF each) filters the output, and R1 over R2 (7.5 kΩ over 10 kΩ) sets 1.05 V from the 0.6 V reference. C4 is the feed-forward capacitor position across R1, suggested for outputs above 2 V. R3 (100 kΩ) pulls EN up to VIN so the converter runs whenever input is present.

notes: Design targets: 20 mV output ripple, 100 mV input ripple, ±5 % output deviation for a 1.5 A load step, 600 kHz.

operation.text: Each device is a 3 A step-down converter with both switches on chip, running from 4.2 V to 17 V in and delivering 0.6 V to 7 V out. The D-CAP3 loop has its compensation inside and an accurate feedback point, and is stable with polymer output capacitors (POSCAP, SP-CAP) and with ceramics whose ESR is close to zero. The converter moves between continuous conduction at heavier load and discontinuous conduction at light load; which light-load behaviour applies depends on the device (Eco-mode on TPS563203, FCCM on TPS563206).

Each switching cycle begins with the high-side MOSFET turning on for a time set by an internal one-shot. That on-time is proportional to VOUT and inversely proportional to VIN, which keeps the frequency nearly constant across the input range. A new cycle begins once FB falls below the reference. An internal ramp summed with the reference takes the place of output ripple, so no ESR ripple is needed and the loop is stable even with almost no ripple at the output; an error amplifier sets the output voltage accurately.

At light load the inductor current valley falls to zero, the boundary between continuous and discontinuous conduction. Below that point the TPS563203 turns the low-side MOSFET off on detecting zero inductor current and runs in discontinuous conduction. The on-time stays near its continuous-mode value, so a smaller load takes longer to discharge the output capacitor to the reference: switching frequency drops in proportion to load current and light-load efficiency stays high. Equation 1 gives the transition current.

The TPS563206 keeps the converter in continuous conduction at light load and lets the inductor current go negative. Its switching frequency stays almost constant across the whole load range, which gives tight control of frequency and output ripple at the price of lower efficiency at light load.

Soft start is internal and lasts 1.4 ms typical: once EN goes high the reference applied to the PWM comparator ramps up. If the output already holds a voltage at start-up, switching and the ramp begin only once the internal reference exceeds VFB, so the output rises smoothly into regulation.

Duty cycle can reach 95 %. When VIN is under 7 V and VFB is below the internal reference, the device lets the switching frequency drop smoothly so the on-time can stretch, holding the output and helping load-transient response. The frequency does not fall below about 200 kHz.

The current limit acts on the valley of the inductor current, cycle by cycle. During the off time the device senses switch current from the low-side FET's drain-source voltage, with temperature compensation. While the sensed current exceeds the OCL level, the low-side FET is held on and no new on-pulse is started, whatever the voltage loop demands; once the current is at or below the limit, switching resumes with a fixed on-time and the same check each cycle. The load current at the limit equals the valley threshold plus half the peak-to-peak ripple. Under limit the output voltage can fall; if FB drops below the UVP threshold, switching stops once the UVP delay has passed and starts again when the hiccup off time ends. Removing the overload returns the output to regulation.

In FCCM the inductor current goes negative at light load, so the TPS563206 watches the current valley against a negative limit. When the valley passes the NOC threshold the low side is switched off and the high side on. After eight NOC events in a row both FETs are switched off; normal switching resumes once the condition clears and the output is back at its target. Too small an inductor triggers NOC and pushes the output above target; Equation 2 gives the minimum inductance.

When FB falls below 60 % (55 % to 65 %) of its target for the 256 µs deglitch time, the device enters hiccup: in a hard short it switches for about 1.5 ms and then stays off for about 13 ms, repeating until the fault clears.

Above the EN on threshold (1.21 V typ) the device switches; below the off threshold (1.00 V typ) it stops. An internal 1 µA current pulls EN low, so the device is off by default. EN can be driven from a divider off VIN, from a voltage under 5.5 V, or tied to VIN through a single pull-up resistor of 100 kΩ. Inside, EN is clamped by a 15 kΩ resistor in series with a 2 V Zener to GND that must not carry much current, so the pull-up from VIN must be no less than 80 kΩ, and no more than 3 MΩ or EN may not reach its on threshold.
UVLO watches the internal regulator voltage and shuts the device off when it is below threshold (VIN wake-up 3.8 V typ, shut-down 3.4 V typ). It does not latch.
The device shuts off when its junction passes about 155 °C and restarts once it has cooled by the 20 °C hysteresis; the protection does not latch.

The internally compensated loop supports a range of output LC filters. At low frequency the loop gain comes from the divider and the internal gain, with 180° phase. Past the LC double pole the gain falls at -40 dB per decade and the phase drops by 180°; an internal high-frequency zero near 41 kHz from the ripple-injection network turns the slope to -20 dB per decade and adds 90° of phase. Choose L and C so the double pole sits near 20 kHz, letting that zero supply the phase margin. Above 2 V output, a feed-forward capacitor across the upper divider resistor (C4, 10 pF to 100 pF) raises bandwidth and phase margin. Keep the loop crossover under fSW / 3. Larger divider resistors improve light-load efficiency, but very large values pick up noise and make errors from FB input current more visible.

Equations 5 to 7 give ripple, peak and RMS inductor current; the saturation rating must exceed the peak and the RMS (heating) rating the RMS value. In the 1.05 V, 3 A design these come to 3.68 A peak and 3.03 A RMS, and the inductor is a Würth 74437349022.

Output ripple depends on capacitance and ESR; the devices are intended for ceramics or similar low-ESR types, and 2 × 22 µF is recommended. In the 1.05 V design two Murata GRM21BR61A226ME44L 22 µF parts are used, each about 2 mΩ ESR and rated 4 A; Equation 8 gives 0.286 A RMS.

Input decoupling is required: a ceramic of more than 10 µF, plus bulk capacitance as the application needs. An extra 0.1 µF (C3) gives more high-frequency filtering and may be left out. Every input capacitor needs a voltage rating above the highest input voltage. The bootstrap capacitor between BST and SW is a 0.1 µF ceramic.
Supply range is 4.2 V to 17 V. The input must sit above the output, and duty cycle tops out at 95 %.

Run VIN and GND as wide copper to cut impedance and spread heat. Mount the input and output capacitors right beside the device, each with plenty of vias. Keep the SW trace short and wide to limit radiated noise, and keep switching current from flowing under the device. Take a separate trace from VOUT to the upper feedback resistor, and return the feedback path to the GND pin by a Kelvin connection. Route the feedback loop away from the switching trace, ideally with ground shielding, keep the FB node small, and give the ground path between the output capacitor and GND a wide trace. In the example layout, VIN and its capacitor sit beside pin 1 with ground vias to a bottom-layer plane, the inductor runs from SW to the output capacitor, the feedback divider sits beside FB, and the bootstrap capacitor sits beside BST and reaches SW through a via and a bottom-layer trace.
